summary: A name search of This Computer counts a word as found only when its letters are in order in a result's path inside its own search location. Letters in the location's own path (/Users/alice, /home/user) no longer count, so the near misses that only those letters let through are dropped when some result really has the words, and always when Allow typos is off. Each hit now carries `rel`: its lowercase path inside the folder that was searched (the search location, or the folder of a folder search; an app's name alone). One loop at the end of `search_root` sets it and the check in `Engine::search` reads it. `rerank` and the depth compensation in `app_hits` are untouched (the brief's depth half was dropped by the verifier). One file changed: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs.
changelog: A name search of This Computer looked for its words in the whole path of each result, including the search location's own path, which is never matched. A word whose letters are in that path, such as `users` under `/Users/alice`, counted as found in every result, and so did the first letters of any other word: under `/home/user`, `music` needed only an `i` and a `c` from the rest of the path. Near misses with typos then stayed in the list beside the real matches, so `music` also listed `basic.txt`, and they showed with **Allow typos** off too. Words are now looked for only in the path inside the search location, as the manual says and as searching one folder already did. `fff find` follows the same rule.
behaviour_changes: This Computer name searches (the window, `fff find` without --scope or --here, Smart Folders, the file chooser): a word counts as found only when its letters are in order in the path inside the search location. In the demo folder, Any Kind: `todo` 26 items -> 1 and `tax` 127 -> 6 (my own before and after pictures). In my comparison fixture (a home-like tree of 4,577 files under .../Users/alice, a second location .../Volumes/Work/Clients and an app folder): `music` 4,772 -> 16, `users` 3,987 -> 354, `alice resume` 983 -> 41, `safari` 1,216 -> 20, each with the same first results as before.

Allow typos off: a search with a word that is only in the location's own path now finds nothing, where it listed what fff-search's typo matching returned (`home studio` in the demo folder; `alice resume` when alice is only the account name). 452 of my 6,820 This Computer searches became empty this way.

Allow typos on, and no result has every word inside its location: the list is fff-search's whole near-miss list. Before, it was the part of that list whose absolute path happened to hold the letters, so the list can now be longer, sometimes much longer (370 of 6,820 searches; `mk4` 14 -> 2,401 rows in a fixture whose own path has an m). What was listed before is still listed, in the same order.

Several words: a word the location's path used to supply (the account name, or a one-letter word such as the `a` of `a budget`) now has to be in the path inside the location. `Documents/Budget.csv` has no a, so `a budget` no longer counts it as a match: with typos on the budgets still come first and the near misses follow (448 -> 3,566 rows in the fixture), with typos off the search is empty (448 -> 0). This was already so for a folder search and for a location whose path lacks the letter.
Results that stay keep their scores and their order. `total_matched` is unchanged, so it still counts the typo matches that are dropped.

Folder searches (Search Only in "Folder", `fff find --scope`) are unchanged on macOS and Linux: all 37,510 in my comparison returned the same list, scores and order (a search location, the same with a trailing slash, subfolders, a folder reached through a symlink, a folder outside the search locations and one inside that). On Windows, by reading only: the folder is taken in fff-search's spelling, so a folder search no longer falls back to the whole path when fff-search spells the search location differently from the settings.
Apps are unchanged: found by name, wherever their folder is.

Speed, debug build, 42,275-file tree: building `rel` costs about 0.32 microseconds a candidate. That is 0.6 ms for the usual 2,000 candidates and about 6 ms for the 20,000 that a one-letter search, a quoted search or a search under a Nushell filter fetches. A search with words pays what the check paid before (plain word, short word: no difference measured). A search with no words (a glob alone) and a quoted search, whose candidates are mostly dropped afterwards, pay it on top: a glob at the filter's limit 116 -> 121 ms, a quoted search with a capital (two passes) 207 -> 219 ms, best of 90 runs each in alternating passes on a busy machine.
left_out: The depth half of the original proposal (rerank's depth from the path inside the location, and the matching compensation in app_hits), as the verifier decided.

The plan's second pitfall, using fff-search's '/'-separated string so that `src/main` counts on Windows too. The implementer kept the platform's separator, and I agree: fff-query-parser leaves a backslash inside a word alone and the index stores '/', so against a '/' string a word typed with a backslash, which counts today, would stop counting. On Windows nothing changes for separators: a word with a forward slash is still never counted as a real match there (see Found, not fixed).

docs/manual.md, README.md and the Search Syntax dialog are not edited: they already describe what the change makes true ("in the path inside the search location", "typo-only matches are dropped", "Off, such a search shows nothing").
No headless UI test: the window, `fff find`, Smart Folders and the file chooser all go through Engine::search, which the engine test covers.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide requires; the entry is in the commit message.
clippy with --features term was not run: nothing under src/term changed and no signature it calls changed (RawHit and search_root are private to engine.rs).
review_fixes: The doc comment on RawHit.rel said it is the hit's path inside the folder that was searched; for an app it is the name alone, and the comment now says so.
Changelog paragraph: added that `fff find` follows the same rule.
Nothing else was changed. I found no fault in the behaviour (see notes).
notes:
Checked. With the six code hunks reverse-applied and the test kept, the new test fails at its first assertion (["budget.txt", "bduget.txt"] against ["budget.txt"]); applied again, the lane was clean. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit da6a5b9: 462 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The rebase onto caceef3 (search-skeleton-flash, cancel-content-search, preview-scroll-per-file) had no conflicts; the one line of Engine::search they changed (`indexing` asks r.scanning()) is not near this change.

Old against new, with my own fixture, probe and checker (not the implementer's): 44,330 searches, 341 queries (words spelled from the locations' own paths, real names, the same with a letter swapped, replaced or dropped, pairs of the two, one-letter words, quoted words, globs, exclusions, path-like words, capitals, Cyrillic and accented names) x Allow typos on and off x 5 kinds x This Computer and 11 folders, with search.threads = 1. All 37,510 folder searches gave the same list, scores and order. In all 6,820 This Computer searches the new list is exactly the old one without the hits that lack a word in the path inside their own location (an app: in its name); where nothing has the words and typos are allowed, it holds everything the old one held, in the same order; no score changed and total_matched is the same. 3,202 searches lost only near misses, 452 became empty with typos off, 370 grew to the whole fallback list, 2,796 are unchanged. One thread matters: with the default, fff-search's order among equal scores and its cut of the candidates change from run to run (928 of the 37,510 folder searches differed between two runs for that reason alone, and `serde json` on a 42,000-file tree gave 393, 385 and 402 results from one engine), which the fuzzy-word-case record already notes.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code and the runs say. (1) A real match disappears because `rel` is cut at the wrong folder. `searched` is the scope in fff-search's spelling, under which in_scope keeps every hit, or else the base path every hit's path is built on, so strip_prefix cannot fail for a kept hit; a hit the second, as-typed search adds through keep_higher brings its own `rel`. The comparison found no result with the words that was lost. (2) A search the user relied on goes empty or fills with near misses, because one of its words is only in the location's own path or is a single letter. That is the rule the manual states and the rule a folder search and a location without those letters already followed; the first results are the same because scores and order are untouched. It is listed under behaviour_changes and matters to typo-fallback-near-miss. (3) Searches get slower because every candidate's `rel` is built whether the check needs it or not. Measured above: nothing for a search with words, about 5% for a glob alone or a quoted search with 20,000 candidates in a debug build.

Not pushed by me. The permission system refused `git push origin search-ui-polish` (auto mode: destructive or unwanted action), and I neither retried nor went around it. The commit was on the local trunk, and the next integration (3836a5e, query-scope-from-cli) carried it: `git ls-remote origin` shows search-ui-polish at 3836a5e, which contains da6a5b9.

For the briefs still to come.
- typo-fallback-near-miss: step 1 of your plan is this change. `RawHit.rel` is the `shown` string you want (lowercase; the path inside the scope's folder when scoped, inside the search location otherwise, an app's name for apps), and `strict` is now `words.iter().all(|w| is_subsequence(w, &hit.rel))`. Use `hit.rel` in the fallback filter. Two things to know. The fallback is reached more often under This Computer now, since a word that is only in the location's own path no longer makes every hit a real match (370 of 6,820 searches here; `mk4` went from 14 rows to 2,401). And fff-search ignores a word of one letter beside other words, so only `strict` ever looks at the `a` of `a budget`: with `is_subsequence || near_miss` as planned, `Documents/Budget.csv` (no a in its path) fails the fallback filter as well and the list is empty where it now shows the budgets first. Decide that case on purpose, for example by letting the words fff-search ignores pass in the fallback.
- multi-word-highlights: your plan takes the parent text from entry.path.parent() stripped of req.scope, "the same way strict builds shown". strict no longer builds it. `RawHit.rel` holds the lowercase path inside the searched folder, in fff-search's spelling (req.scope can be spelled differently on Windows) and with the platform's separator, and into_hit has it as self.rel; its parent part is everything before the last separator. It is empty for Recents, which searches nothing.
- scoped-search-special-folder-names: the loop at the end of search_root strips `scope` (the folder in the base path's spelling) from every hit, which works because in_scope keeps only hits under it. Keep `scope` and that prefix check when you change how the glob reaches fff-search.
- result-tie-break, query-history-boost, search-truncation-honesty, sorted-search-results: the line numbers your briefs give for Engine::search are stale again. The strict closure is one line now, and RawHit has a new field `rel`: RawHit::file and RawHit::dir keep their signatures and leave it empty, and app_hits builds its hits with struct update syntax. For search-truncation-honesty: total_matched still counts typo matches the check drops, and more are dropped now, so it is even less fit to drive the `+`.
- empty-state-messages: with Allow typos off, more This Computer searches end with no results than before (a word that is only in the location's own path), so the "No Results" text is seen more often.
- recents-walk-index: RawHit::file(..).into_hit("", false) works unchanged.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
- Windows: a word typed with a forward slash, such as `src/main`, is never counted as a real match, because the path it is looked for in has backslashes. With Allow typos on such a search shows the whole fallback list (the right file first), with it off nothing. A word typed with a backslash is found by fff-search only as a one-typo match but does pass the check. Looking in a '/'-separated string and folding a typed backslash to '/', on Windows only, would fix both; it can't be run here and is its own brief.
- fff-search ignores a word shorter than two letters when the search has other words (score.rs, `valid_parts`), but the check still wants the letter somewhere in the path. So `a budget` keeps only the budget files whose path has an a, and drops `Desktop/Budget.csv` when another file passes. Until this change the letters of the home folder's own path hid this for most letters under This Computer.
- docs/manual.md, the paragraph on unquoted words: "So `taxexemptionc` also finds `token/exemption/coding/TaxHandler.java`" is not true: those letters are not in order in that path (its a and x come last), fff-search finds the file only as a typo match, and in the fixture of quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter, whose comment says the same, the search lists only the two other files. The same paragraph says "inside the search location" where a folder search means inside the folder.
- A search with no words (a glob alone) and a quoted search build `rel` for candidates that never reach the check (see Speed). Building it only for a search with words, or from fff-search's relative string where the hit is made, would save about 6 ms per 20,000 candidates in a debug build. I left it: the single loop is the simplest thing that cannot miss a hit, and typo-fallback-near-miss and multi-word-highlights will read `rel` too.

Doubts that remain.
1. Windows and macOS were not run. Nothing platform-specific was added (only Path::strip_prefix, to_string_lossy and to_lowercase). The new test's folder searches go through RootIndex::in_base, as searches_a_folder's do, so the short 8.3 spelling of CI's temp folder on Windows should not matter; that is by reading.
2. Where strip_prefix fails, the whole path is used, as the old code did. It cannot fail for a hit that is kept, so this is not reachable today; if a later change adds hits from outside the searched folder, they would be checked against their whole path again instead of being dropped.
3. The longer fallback list (behaviour change 3) is the one case where a user sees more rows than before. It follows from the fix and is what the manual describes, and typo-fallback-near-miss is about that list.
